title: Azure Cache for Redis: tiers and clustering

videos.script: Quitanda's product pages ask Cosmos DB for the same few hundred products all day. {{pages}} A cache keeps a copy of those answers in memory, and most requests never reach the database. On Azure that cache is Redis, run by Microsoft. {{redis}} There are two services with that job. Azure Cache for Redis is the older one, and Microsoft has announced its retirement. Azure Managed Redis is the one to choose today. {{services}} No emulator answers either of them. So this lesson runs Redis itself in a container, the engine both services are built on. {{local}} You will write the usual pattern in Python. Ask the cache first. On a miss, ask the database, and keep the answer for five minutes. {{aside}} Then you will break it. A price changes in the database, and the page keeps showing the old one. {{stale}} You will fill the cache to its limit and watch the eviction policy decide what it throws away. {{evict}} And you will see how a clustered cache splits its keys into sixteen thousand slots, and why two keys sometimes have to share one. {{slots}}
